matches.rationale: GT1 concerns the incorrect ordering and improper definition of orthogonal matrices in Equation (1) (ISVD encryption step). None of the findings address Equation (1) or the ISVD encryption logic; the findings focus on other equations and issues.
GT2 identifies an ill-formed matrix multiplication in Equation (5) for leverage scores (e_{i,j}^T multiplied by U_k). No finding discusses Equation (5) or leverage score computation issues.

GT3 concerns unclear specification of replay buffer allocation across clients and baselines in Section 5.1 and Tables 2-3. While pred_id 3 identifies data inconsistencies in Tables 2 and 4, it does not address the experimental design protocol issue of memory budget allocation or baseline comparison fairness.

GT4 concerns missing variance/standard deviation for TinyImageNet results in Tables 2 and 3. Pred_id 3 identifies numerical inconsistencies between tables but does not mention missing variance metrics or statistical significance issues.

GT5 identifies exaggerated claims of 'adaptability and robustness' in Section 5.2 despite marginal/uneven gains. Pred_id 4 directly matches this by showing the abstract/Section 5.4 claims of '2%-15% improvement' and 'consistently outperforms' contradict Table 2 data showing FedCBDR underperforms LANDER in one case.
GT6 concerns fabricated or unverifiable future references ([5], [6], [8], [12], [13]) in Related Work. No finding addresses reference fabrication or citation issues.
GT7 concerns missing ethical approval statements, consent, or privacy safeguards in the Experiments section. No finding discusses ethical integrity or IRB approval omissions.

GT8 identifies overpromising rhetoric in the Abstract claiming FedCBDR 'achieves balanced class-wise sampling' and 'improves generalization' without qualifiers. Pred_id 4 captures the same issue by showing the abstract's universal improvement claims contradict actual experimental results.

GT9 identifies misalignment between the Conclusion's claim of 'significantly improves final performance' and the Experiments showing marginal/mixed results. Pred_id 4 demonstrates this cross-section contradiction by showing abstract/conclusion claims conflict with Table 2 data.

GT10 concerns selective omission and inconsistent reporting in Tables 2, 3, and 5 (missing variance, underreported baselines). Pred_id 3 identifies data integrity issues in Tables 2 and 4 with inconsistent numerical values and missing data, matching the core concern of selective/inconsistent reporting.

GT11 identifies inconsistent temperature scaling formulations between Equations (7) and (9) in Section 4.2, with unclear concatenations and notation. Pred_id 1 directly matches this by documenting that Eq. (7) and Eq. (9) present mathematically distinct loss functions (separate vs joint softmax normalization).

GT12 concerns overstated claims about TTS module effectiveness in Section 5.3/Table 4 despite marginal gains within variance. While pred_id 3 identifies data inconsistencies in Table 4, it does not address the claim interpretation distortion about TTS module contributions.

GT13 concerns missing details on baseline hyperparameter tuning methodology, computational budgets, and resource trade-offs in Section 5.1. No finding addresses experimental protocol transparency or baseline tuning methodology.

GT14 concerns selective omission of poor-performing hyperparameter settings in Section 5.6 sensitivity analysis. No finding discusses hyperparameter sensitivity analysis or selective reporting of parameter settings.

GT15 identifies inconsistency between the Abstract's claim of 'global coordination mechanism' and the Method's actual privacy-constrained pseudo-feature aggregation. While pred_id 2 discusses normalization issues in the GDR module, it does not address the abstract-method narrative misalignment about global perspective capabilities.
